facts.text: Goodrich was incorporated as a village in 1957 while still closely tied to the surrounding Atlas Township.
The village’s name comes from early settler John Goodrich, who arrived in the area in 1835 after traveling from Buffalo to Detroit.
Goodrich sits within Atlas Township and is part of the Flint metropolitan area, linking it to a larger regional community.
Early settlers noted the land’s rich, fertile soil, abundant timber, and plentiful water when they reached what is now Goodrich.
Despite ups and downs downtown, Goodrich has maintained a strong community spirit with active volunteer groups and generous fundraising for schools, the library, and churches.
Goodrich’s residents enjoy a rural lifestyle, with 100% of the population living in non-urban areas according to the latest census data.
